chapter: Early bands and the city, c. 1898-1900s
title: Professor Ullett, Cantrell and Willie Umford clarinet lessons
summary: Tom recalls playing with old professor Ullett, drummer Cantrell and his clarinetist son, and taking two clarinet lessons from old man Umford.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Old professor Ullett. He was one of the owners, one of the years used to play violin. I called him Ullett. I played with them. Cantrell used to play drums, a fellow called Cantrell, used to play drums with him. But I know his son.
His son is a clarinet player.
Yeah. I don't know his son, no.
I know him. Well you all lived where? What part of town was you? Well in the French part of the town, yeah, downtown there. Yeah.
But he was an old professor. Yeah.

And this boy there, his father, I went to the school, and I went to the school, and I picked up clarinet, but I put it down. I went and took two lessons with Willie Umford, the old man Umford, that's his father. Willie Umford's boys, Percy, Umford, and Willie. He played yesterday or day.
